headline: Polymer and sequence-design models probe how DNA sequence shapes 3D chromatin folding
label: Chromatin Polymer Structure Modeling
summary: Coarse-grained and data-driven polymer models now link chromatin fluctuations and sequence design to 3D genome folding.
synthesis: The dominant thread is physics-based polymer modeling of genome organization. A data-driven polymer model attributes chromatin organization to scale-dependent active fluctuations, tying the polymer's properties to its function. Akita Semifreddo extends this framing toward design: a half-frozen AkitaV2 genome folding model paired with the Ledidi optimizer generates ~2 kb DNA sequences with programmed three-dimensional genome folding. RNA2PS, a sequence-specific coarse-grained RNA model, is the most distant item. It connects structure, nearest-neighbour thermodynamics and phase separation, and shares the coarse-grained, sequence-resolved modeling approach rather than the chromatin context. What is new across the set is the pairing of sequence-resolved coarse-grained models with predictive or design-oriented use.
